draftBefore.emotion: affectionate and informal, often used when speaking to someone younger or close
notes: This word has two very different uses. It is first an animal, but it is also a very common personal pronoun. In casual conversation, Thai speakers often use 'หนู' to refer to themselves when speaking to someone older, a superior, or in a gentle, informal setting.
Be careful: using 'หนู' as a pronoun can sound quite youthful or childlike. Only use it if you are close to the listener or want to sound humble and polite.
